subject: Latency & cost guardrails + buying path for Atlas Health
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Alex Gomez <agomez@atlashealth.com>
Cc:  
Date: 2027-04-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap: perf targets, stakeholders, and next steps

Hi Alex — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and asks so we can keep momentum: 

Summary of what we heard
- Primary use: real-time clinical decision support (low-latency scoring from patient notes, mixed-length prompts ~128–512 tokens)
- Deployment preference: VPC/private deployment due to PHI (you mentioned your security team will want on-prem/VPC options)
- Decision window: target Q3 procurement decision; pilot to start late May

Clarifying questions / asks for the buying process (can you confirm these?):
1) Economic buyer: who signs for capex/commitment (you mentioned Emily Park on the call) — can you confirm full name + best email?
2) Procurement & legal: who will run the PoC/MOU/contract redlines? You mentioned Samuel Price in procurement — please confirm contact and cadence.
3) Security evidence: will SOC 2 + network architecture + data flow diagrams be sufficient, or do you need a formal DPA/HIPAA addendum up front?
4) Latency & cost targets: do you have hard targets for P95 latency and cost per inference? In the call you said P95 around ~150ms is ideal. Please confirm whether that is a hard SLO.

Immediate next steps I propose:
- Ben and Marissa from our team will prepare a short decision-grade brief: deployment options (hosted vs dedicated vs private), expected p95 estimates for 128/512 tokens, and a pilot pricing proposal.
- We’ll attach a one-pager SLA summary and a short decision-guardrails deck.

If you can confirm the procurement contact and the economic buyer, Ben/Marissa and I will map out a mutual action plan and send a proposed pilot statement of work.

Thanks — talk soon,
Karthik

--
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com

From: Alex Gomez <agomez@atlashealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Emily Park <epark@atlashealth.com>, Samuel Price <sprice@atlashealth.com>
Date: 2027-04-18T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: perf targets, stakeholders, and next steps

Thanks Karthik — helpful summary. A few clarifications from our end: 

1) Economic buyer: Yes — Emily Park (CFO). Use epark@atlashealth.com for approvals.
2) Procurement: Samuel Price (Director, Procurement) will own the contract and scope. sprice@atlashealth.com. He'll want to run a quick procurement checklist before legal redlines.
3) Security: We handle PHI; SOC 2 + DPA with a HIPAA addendum will be required before production. Our security team will ask for network diagrams and a runbook for key management (KMS/HSM).
4) Latency: P95 <= 150ms for 128-token interactions is a hard request for the initial pilot. For 512-token inference we can accept P95 <= 300ms, but lower is better. These targets are for our US region traffic.
5) Cost guardrail: we have an internal target to keep inference costs under $0.30 per 1k-token-equivalent during pilot, but we are flexible if the pilot demonstrates value.

Pilot scope idea: 2-week private/VPC pilot with 1-2 model variants, can be staged to dedicated if performance looks good. Samuel — can you advise on the procurement checklist items you want early?

Happy to jump on a quick follow-up with procurement/security next week.

—Alex
Alex Gomez
Director, Applied ML | Atlas Health
agomez@atlashealth.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Alex Gomez <agomez@atlashealth.com>, Emily Park <epark@atlashealth.com>, Samuel Price <sprice@atlashealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-19T10:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: perf targets, stakeholders, and next steps

Alex / Emily / Samuel — great, thanks for the clarity. I've looped in Marissa (solutions lead) and Ben (commercial) to put numbers and an operational plan behind this. Two quick items: 

A) We attached two docs: "redwood-decision-guardrails.pdf" (deployment options, expected P95 estimates for 128/512 tokens per model family, quantization and batching tradeoffs) and "redwood-sla-summary.pdf" (SLA options for hosted/dedicated/private). Those are attached to this thread.
B) Pilot proposal (high-level):
- Duration: 2–3 weeks
- Mode: Private VPC deployment (customer-managed VPC peering), option to switch to Dedicated pool after pilot
- Targets: P95 <= 150ms (128 tokens) and P95 <= 300ms (512 tokens)
- Deliverables: perf runbook, cost estimation for expected throughput, SOC2 evidence, DPA + HIPAA addendum draft

Samuel — for procurement checklist, examples that speed approvals: SOW + PoC acceptance criteria, a standard data flow diagram, and a pilot pricing memo (shows committed vs overage rates). If you share a procurement template, we'll slot the fields in.

Next steps I propose:
1) Samuel: share procurement checklist and typical contract turnaround (days)
2) Emily: confirm economic buyer's preferred approval cadence (one-time sign vs staged approvals)
3) Atlas security: share the contact for the security evidence intake (or forward us the questionnaire)
4) Redwood (Marissa/Ben/Karthik): deliver pilot SOW + short pricing memo by Tue 2027-04-20 EOD PST

I added links to a short demo recording for context: https://app.redwood.com/demo/recordings/ATL-042-call

Thanks all — we'll get the SOW drafted and include a recommended pilot SLA and pricing that aims to meet your cost guardrail.

Regards,
Karthik

Attachments: redwood-decision-guardrails.pdf, redwood-sla-summary.pdf

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-20T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: perf targets, stakeholders, and next steps

Karthik / Marissa — internal quick plan after Alex's notes: 

1) Pricing approach for pilot: propose a fixed 3-week pilot fee (covers reserved capacity + support) + usage overage priced to hit their $0.30/1k-token guardrail at our forecasted throughput. We'll offer a short-term credit if P95 targets aren't met during pilot.
2) Technical ask: Marissa to lead the perf estimates; call out tradeoffs: quantized 4-bit vs 8-bit, batching window to balance latency, and KV cache strategy for repeated prompts.
3) Contract/process: request Samuel's procurement checklist. If they want NDA + DPA + HIPAA addendum, route to legal immediately.

Deliverables & owners by EOD 2027-04-20:
- Pilot SOW + acceptance criteria (Ben)
- Cost forecast and pricing memo (Ben)
- Perf estimates and deployment doc (Marissa)
- Draft DPA addendum template to Legal (Karthik)

I'll draft the pricing memo and send to Karthik for review before we send to Atlas. Low-risk recommendation: offer a single-week extension option if they need extra time to validate (at pre-negotiated rate).

Ben
